gabarito.reason:
This is a false positive. The flagged GCMParameterSpec is built in SecretEncryption.decrypt (commons/src/androidMain/.../SecretEncryption.android.kt:174-177). On decrypt, the IV has to be the one the data was encrypted with. Here that is the first 12 bytes of the stored blob, so by design it does not come from a random source at that point. The IV is generated randomly where it matters, in encrypt(). That method calls cipher.init(ENCRYPT_MODE, key) without passing any parameters, so the AndroidKeyStore provider creates a fresh random 12-byte nonce. The method reads it from cipher.iv and writes iv + ciphertext. The key comes from KeyGenParameterSpec with no setRandomizedEncryptionRequired(false), so randomized encryption stays required by default. The keystore would actually reject an IV supplied by the caller on encrypt, which means the code cannot reuse a nonce under this key. The JVM/desktop version (SecretEncryption.jvm.kt) works the same way. RVSec flagged decrypt only because its rule expects a random-source IV for every GCMParameterSpec and does not track that this IV is the provider-generated one from encrypt. A PR that "randomized" the decrypt IV would make every value already stored unreadable.

Delivery policy (v3, the same for every unit): a pull request, an issue and no action are all acceptable deliveries; judge each on its quality, not on whether it should have been sent. A pull request that changes the code only so that it satisfies the specification, without changing behaviour, is acceptable when it is correct, keeps every must_not_break constraint and does not present itself as a vulnerability fix; do not mark it down as unnecessary churn or because the finding is a false positive. Do not guess whether the runtime checker would still report the patched code; judge the code.
must_not_break: The stored format is a 12-byte GCM IV prefix followed by the AES-GCM ciphertext and 128-bit tag. decrypt must keep reading the IV from the stored bytes, or data already stored can no longer be decrypted.

Data encrypted at rest through SecretEncryption must stay decryptable. This covers EncryptedDataStore, AccountSecretsEncryptedStores, AccountRosterStore, StoreAccountSessionStore, the Marmot MLS group-state, KeyPackage, message and publish-obligation stores, and the Cordn blob cipher. Users would otherwise lose their keys or sessions.

The existing AndroidKeyStore key (alias AMETHYST_AES_KEY, StrongBox or TEE, randomized encryption required) must keep working. Passing a caller-chosen IV on encrypt, or recreating the key, would make the keystore reject the call or orphan existing data.
On encrypt, the provider must keep generating a random nonce per call, so a nonce is never reused under the key.
The desktop/JVM key file secret.key and its IV-prefixed format, which mirror the Android version, must stay as they are.
Thread-local Cipher use and cachedKey invalidation when a call fails must stay as they are.

Continue decrypting existing records formatted as a 12-byte IV followed by GCM ciphertext and its 128-bit authentication tag, including Base64-wrapped EncryptedDataStore values and encrypted Marmot files.
Preserve the original stored IV during decryption. Randomizing or replacing it would cause authentication failures and make account secrets, messages and MLS state unreadable.

Preserve the existing AMETHYST_AES_KEY alias and AndroidKeyStore protection, including StrongBox where available and the regular fallback on supported devices; replacing the key would strand stored data.

Keep provider-generated fresh IVs for encryption, GCM authentication and failure propagation for invalid ciphertext. Replacing GCMParameterSpec with IvParameterSpec would break the AndroidKeyStore GCM path.
